cells.tense: The felt-sense of fairness is here, holding the pen in the present.
cells.ask: Name what the clearing gave you, then keep one piece of it that is plainly yours.
cells.core:
When a false structure drops, there is no need to build a replacement the same day. The reading is steady here, and a steady reading can choose from what is actually on the ground. The old shape can be gone without the space being filled, and whatever the fall left behind that is yours can be picked up without a case being made for it.

Name what the clearing gave you, then keep one piece that is plainly yours. Not the whole yield and not a report for anyone. What is kept can sit in the open without a ledger attached. Fairness as a felt thing does not ask for a sum; it asks that the ground that moved be described as it is, and that what survived be allowed to be yours.
cells.sheetLine: Count what the clearing left you and keep one true piece.

cells.tense: A future that must come out right keeps you braced ahead of any clearing.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Fill one actual gap the changed ground opened for someone near you, all the way through.
cells.core:
Braced for a future that cannot be written yet, the compass turns loud. Each way of being fair starts demanding proof, and strength gets handed over before it is asked for. Help arrives carrying a verdict, and the person who only wanted a hand ends up holding more than they asked for.

One actual gap that the changed ground opened for someone near you — fill it all the way through, then set the job down. Not their whole future, not a claim on being needed. A concrete piece of help, finished, can stand as a fact that needs no defense. The future is still unwritten when the job is done, but the moved day is real, and strength that contains rather than crushes leaves nothing owed on either side.
cells.sheetLine: Fill one real gap and see it through.

cells.tense: You are still standing in a doorway the clearing has already carried you past.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Take the way you already know with one person who is lost on it, and go the stretch alongside them.
cells.core:
The clear route through the structure that fell is visible from where you stand, and the asking keeps sending you back to the doorway to check whether you really went through. What is fair gets relitigated against hours that already happened, and the compass stays busy proving what was not in question.

Take the way you know with one person who is lost on it, and go the stretch alongside them. A sentence and a walk, a message and a call ahead. Walking it with one person is a full act, and the same clarity is not owed to a whole list of people. The route is real even when the past keeps asking for evidence, and moving along it is also how the one moving finds footing again while the going stays shared.
cells.sheetLine: Walk the route you know with the one who's lost.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where the felt-sense of fairness already writes.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: Let two pulls on you stay true at once, then take up both this week instead of picking between.
cells.core:
The reading is already weighing true against false, and the hours get spent as if chance were doing the weighing. Several pulls arrive at once — what is owed, what someone needs, what was left unsaid — and the next hour is spent as if each had the same claim on it. They do not, and this has been going on without a hand on the page.

Let two pulls on you stay true at once, then take up both this week instead of picking one to the exclusion of the other. What is owed to a friend and what you want for yourself can both hold weight without either getting demoted. The missing piece is only that the one doing the work has not yet put a name to doing it, and putting a name to it is the work.
cells.sheetLine: Two things can be true. Take up both.
